name: Sarecycline

fda.text: 5 WARNINGS AND PRECAUTIONS The use of SEYSARA during tooth development (second and third trimesters of pregnancy, infancy, and childhood up to the age of 8 years) may cause permanent discoloration of the teeth (yellow-gray-brown). ( 5.1 ) If Clostridium difficile Associated Diarrhea (antibiotic associated colitis)…

summary: Using Sarecycline while teeth are still forming, such as during the middle to late stages of pregnancy or in children under 8 years old, can permanently turn teeth a yellow-gray-brown color [3]. Another warning notes the risk of severe diarrhea linked to an infection known as Clostridium difficile associated diarrhea, or swelling of the large intestine caused by antibiotics [3]. Additionally, results from a small computer model rather than human tests give the drug a medium score for liver risk and a low score for heart risk [M].
